title: Faxian's journey
hookLine: read a chapter of Faxian's record (Legge)
tomorrow: ten pictures of a lost ox. which one are you in?

cards: The trip is booked, the bag's half packed, and the homesickness shows up early, before you've even left. A monk named Faxian set out from China for India, much of it on foot, and his journey took years. So why go at all?
He tells us in his opening lines. The rules of monastic discipline in China were broken and incomplete, and he set out to find them.

teach.b: His record is plain and vivid. First the desert: no birds overhead, no animals on the ground, and the only way to find the route is the dry bones of the dead.
Then the snowy mountains, where a companion dies of the cold, and Faxian weeps over him.

teach.h: THE PLACES OF THE BUDDHA'S LIFE.
teach.b: In India he walks to the places where the Buddha's life happened, the same places the Buddha, in his last days, named as worth a visit: where he was born, woke up, first taught, and passed away.
And he finds what he came for. He stays to learn the language and copy out the rules by hand. Then the moment people remember.

In Sri Lanka, a long way from home, his companions gone, he sees a merchant offer a white silk fan from China at a temple, and he can't hold back his tears. The sea voyage home, with its storms, is still ahead of him.
That's what pilgrimage means in Buddhism: you walk toward the source, and you carry something back for the people at home.
Faxian's gift was the rules his community lacked.

how: Buddhists still go on pilgrimage to the places of the Buddha's life that he named in his last days, and many pilgrims bring home something for their community: water, a leaf, a text, a story.

games.why: Faxian walked toward the source to bring back what his community lacked. a pilgrimage, in his record, ends at home.

practice: Name one place you would go for what it means, not for the view: a temple, a grandparent's town, a quiet spot near home. Then name what stands in the way, and one small first step.
Sit with all three: the place, the obstacle, the step.
